assays.assay_description: Mice injected i.p. with saline or drug (DOI, 2C-T-7, DPT, or DIPT), then placed into an observation cage with fresh bedding. Ten minutes post-injection, an overhead camera recorded behavior for 10 minutes; videotapes were scored for HTR by a blind observer. Used for acute dose-effect, tolerance (daily, every other day, weekly), and cross-tolerance studies.

application_type.evidence: Doses were then calculated and prepared for intraperitoneal injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: Individual animals were removed from the home cage, injected... and then placed into an observation cage containing fresh bedding.

setup_restrain.evidence: placed into an observation cage containing fresh bedding

food_restriction.evidence: No food or water was available during experimental sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: No food or water was available during experimental sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: Ten minutes after this injection, an overhead camera was activated and behavior was recorded for 10 minutes.

sample_size.evidence: Mice were randomly assigned to experimental groups (n = 5 or 6 per group)

outcomes.summary: All four hallucinogens produced dose-dependent biphasic increases in head twitches (DOI, 2C-T-7 maximal at 1.0 mg/kg; DPT at 3.0 mg/kg; DIPT only significant at 10.0 mg/kg). Daily administration of DOI or 2C-T-7 produced progressive tolerance over 5 days, while DPT and DIPT did not induce tolerance. DOI tolerance was insurmountable by higher DOI doses, and DOI pretreatment produced cross-tolerance to both 2C-T-7 and DPT.
outcomes.evidence: Progressive tolerance to DOI-elicited HTR developed with daily administration of 1.0 mg/kg... HTR elicited by daily administration of 3.0 mg/kg DPT or 10.0 mg/kg DIPT did not change over the treatment interval.

B1_num_measures.evidence: videotapes were scored for drug-elicited HTR (defined as a rapid rotational jerk of the head)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Ordinates show the mean head twitches recorded over a 10-minute observation period.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Only total head twitch counts reported; no transitions or sequences.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR (defined as a rapid rotational jerk of the head that can be distinguished from species-appropriate grooming or scratching behaviors)

B5_social.evidence: individual animals were removed from the home cage... placed into an observation cage

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is a reflexive 5-HT2A-mediated response; no learning component.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: videotapes were scored... by at least one observer blind to drug treatment.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Injections were administered every 24 hours for 5 days (all compounds), every other day for five total injections (DOI only), or every 7 days for four total injections (DOI only).

D5_followup.evidence: All recordings occurred shortly (10 min) after drug administration; no post-acute drug-free follow-up.

judge_notes: Both candidates identified a single HTR assay; merged consistent with rubric (acute dose-effect + tolerance + cross-tolerance = one HTR paradigm).
Set schedule='multiple' for DOI/2C-T-7/DPT because each compound was used both in single-dose (acute) and repeated daily dosing (5 days = repeated); DIPT only tested repeatedly.
Scored B1 as 0 (single measure: head twitch count) following qwen; HTR is one variable.
Day_night_flipped scored 'no' because the paper explicitly identifies testing in the light phase under a standard 12:12 cycle.
